input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers per-project idle-resource reporting in the RHOAI web
console. Cluster administrators get a single reporting surface per project
showing (a) idle workbenches — last activity, owner, and reserved resources —
sourced from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking, and
(b) stale pipeline runs — completed runs older than a configurable age with
retained artifacts — sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. Either
report can be exported as CSV so admins can act on the data outside the
console. No new data collection is built: both source systems already track
the needed metadata; this epic surfaces it.

## Scope

- New per-project idle-resource reporting surface in the RHOAI web console
  (navigation and view), visible to cluster administrators.
- Idle-workbench report: per workbench in the project, show last activity
  (sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking), owner, and
  reserved resources.
- Stale pipeline-run report: list completed pipeline runs older than a
  configurable age that still retain artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow
  Pipelines run metadata.
- Configurable staleness age threshold for the pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report, matching the displayed data.
- Read-only consumption of the notebook controller and Kubeflow Pipelines
  data — no code changes in those components; they must keep working
  unchanged (validated as part of this epic's testing).
- Out of scope: automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources,
  cost/chargeback calculations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, when an administrator opens the
  idle-resource report for that project, then the console displays each
  workbench's last activity (sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking), its owner, and its reserved resources.
- Given a project containing pipeline runs, when an administrator opens the
  stale pipeline-run report for that project, then the console lists
  completed runs older than the configured age that retain artifacts,
  sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- The staleness age threshold is configurable, and changing it changes which
  runs appear in the stale pipeline-run report.
- Either report can be exported as CSV, and the exported file matches the
  data displayed in the console for that report.
- The notebook controller and Kubeflow Pipelines continue to operate without
  modification while the reports consume their existing data (no code
  changes land in those components; existing functionality is not regressed).
- The console's build pipeline and tests are green with the new reporting
  surface included.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking — delivered by the idle-workbench report above.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata — delivered by the stale pipeline-run report above.
- **HLR-3 (P2, bundled)**: CSV export of either report — bundled here because
  it is an action on the same report surface and data the P1 reports build;
  splitting it out would force a second pass over the same console surface.

# Idle resource reporting documentation

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation for the RHOAI web console's
idle-resource reporting capability: what the idle-workbench and stale
pipeline-run reports show, where to find them, how to configure the staleness
age, how to export them as CSV, and the safe reclamation steps an
administrator should follow to reclaim capacity from idle workbenches and
stale pipeline runs. The documentation is written once the console reporting
capability is implemented, so it describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- New/updated documentation topic introducing the per-project idle-resource
  reports in the RHOAI web console: purpose (reclaiming capacity with
  confidence) and where the reports appear in the console.
- Idle-workbench report documentation: the fields shown (last activity,
  owner, reserved resources), where the data comes from (notebook controller
  activity tracking), and how to interpret it.
- Stale pipeline-run report documentation: what "stale" means (completed runs
  older than the configured age with retained artifacts), how to configure
  the age threshold, and the data source (Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata).
- How to export either report as CSV.
- Safe reclamation steps: manual, administrator-controlled steps for
  reclaiming capacity from idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs
  (including artifact cleanup considerations), consistent with the strategy's
  out-of-scope boundary — automated reclamation and cost/chargeback are not
  documented as features.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports, the fields each displays,
  and where in the console to find them.
- Published documentation explains the configurable staleness age for the
  stale pipeline-run report and how to change it.
- Published documentation explains how to export either report as CSV.
- Published documentation includes safe reclamation steps covering both idle
  workbenches and stale pipeline runs, clearly scoped to manual reclamation.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented console
  reports so every described field, control, and step matches the shipped
  behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation
  steps — delivered by the content outline above.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9016 (Idle resource reporting in the web console)

## Triage Note

The strategy has a single active component (the RHOAI web console / Dashboard,
owned by one team) and no open questions, which would normally make it a

a distinct work stream with its own review cycle — so the below-threshold
escape applies and the strategy received a full decomposition.

  derived from architecture context.
- **High Level Requirements**: HLR-1 (P1, idle-workbench report), HLR-2 (P1,

- **Staff Engineer Input**: absent — AI-generated content used as-is.

Canonical component mappings (from `.context/rhai-components.txt`):

| Strategy name | Canonical component | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | Active (epic E001) |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Passive — validation folded into E001 ACs |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | Passive — validation folded into E001 ACs |

All three components exist in `.context/architecture-context/`
(`architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`, `notebooks.md`,
`data-science-pipelines.md`) — no new-component onboarding chains are needed,

Passive-component handling: the strategy states the data already exists

Epic boundary rationale: HLR-1 and HLR-2 are both P1 work on the same
component (Dashboard), same team (RHOAI Dashboard), and the same logical
change — the strategy's problem statement asks for "a single report … showing
idle and stale resources per project", i.e. one per-project reporting surface
in the console. Splitting the two reports into separate epics would have both
epics build the same report surface and CSV-export plumbing independently, so
they stay in one epic. Documentation (HLR-4) is a separate work-product type
(docs content authoring) and a separate component, so it is its own


  stale pipeline-run) if either backend data integration exceeds ~1.5 weeks
  of estimated effort, or if implementation reveals the two reports ship on
  separate console pages/surfaces rather than one reporting surface.

  resources" for workbenches — the strategy does not define which reservations

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing. Both data
sources are in-platform, GA components.
